Beállítom Vlagyimir Putyin orosz elnök kedden telefonon egyeztetett Donald Trump amerikai elnökkel, a beszélgetés pontosan egy órán át tartott. A Kreml közlése szerint a két elnök az orosz–ukrán háború lezárásának lehetőségeit vitatta meg. A beszélgetésről Jurij Usakov, az orosz elnök külpolitikai tanácsadója számolt be. Szerinte a tárgyalás „konstruktív és őszinte” volt – írta az Interfax orosz hírügynökség. Steve Witkoff amerikai különmegbízott és Jared Kushner, Donald Trump veje a hétvégén előbb Moszkvában találkozott Putyinnal , majd Kijevbe utaztak , ahol Volodimir Zelenszkij ukrán elnökkel tárgyaltak. A látogatások célja az volt, hogy előremozdítsák az elakadt tárgyalásokat, de igazán nagy áttörést nem sikerült elérni a látogatásokkal. Usakov szerint Putyin ismertette Trumppal, hogyan látja a háború jelenlegi helyzetét és a harctéri kilátásokat. Azt is felvázolta, hogy Oroszország szerint az Egyesült Államok milyen lépésekkel járulhatna hozzá a harcok mielőbbi lezárásához. A Kreml szerint Putyin pozitívan értékelte Trump és az amerikai kormány közvetítői erőfeszítéseit. A Reuters beszámolója szerint az orosz elnök egyértelművé tette, hogy Oroszországnak nincsenek ellenséges tervei Európával szemben. „Donald Trump egyértelműen hangsúlyozta, hogy kívánatos a konfliktus mielőbbi lezárása, ami azonnal lenyűgöző kilátásokat nyitna az Egyesült Államok és Oroszország közötti kapcsolatok teljes helyreállítására” – mondta Usakov. „Véleménye szerint ez különösen a kereskedelmi és gazdasági kapcsolatokra lenne hatással, és hatalmas előnyöket ígérne mindkét ország számára. Donald Trump szívesen látná, ha elnöksége alatt áttörés történne. Vlagyimir Putyin támogatta ezt a megközelítést” – tette hozzá az orosz elnök tanácsadója. Putyin és Trump abban is egyetértettek, hogy folytatni kell a fogolycseréket. A két elnök abban állapodott meg, hogy kapcsolatban maradnak, és szükség esetén ismét egyeztetnek egymással. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c54g.text: Image source, Reuters Image caption, Tobias Rausch easily won the vote with the backing of nine MPs beyond his own party By Paul Kirby Europe digital editor Published 6 October 2026 A month after Germany's far-right AfD scored a decisive victory in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt, the party's candidate Tobias Rausch has been elected as parliament speaker there too. Not since World War Two has a far-right party secured the post of speaker, and protesters outside the building in Magdeburg held up banners saying, "Never again is now". Although the AfD fell three seats short of a majority in last month's election, Rausch, 35, comfortably won Tuesday's vote with the support of 9 MPs from other parties. "The days of political firewalls should be a thing of the past," Rausch said after the vote, rejecting a post-war consensus in German politics not to work with the far right. This was the first time since last month's state vote that Saxony-Anhalt's newly elected representatives had gathered in parliament, and regional Greens party leader Susan Sziborra-Seidlitz said "a line has been crossed" with the election of a far-right speaker of parliament, and it was a watershed moment. "We will not let ourselves be intimidated, and we will not sit by when rights are curtailed either here or for people in the state," she said. The AfD is considered pro-Russian and anti-immigrant, with plans to segregate child refugees in schools, as well as intolerant towards the LGBT community. Within Saxony-Anhalt it is also classed as "right-wing extremist" by domestic intelligence, a description rejected by party leaders. Until now its members have sat on the right fringe of the state parliament, but ahead of Tuesday's inaugural session it successfully argued that it should now sit in the centre. Image source, Reuters Image caption, As the AfD's Ulrich Siegmund spoke to reporters, protesters held up a sign saying "2026. Never again is now." Rausch, a trained estate agent, has been a member of the parliament for 10 years and he is seen as a close confidant of local AfD leader Ulrich Siegmund, a charismatic figure who is now seeking to become state premier in December. His new role is largely symbolic, but Rausch will now chair debates, have the power to control access to the parliament building and represent parliament at official events. Although his victory was secured by five MPs from the hard-left BSW, there was surprise that four other unidentified MPs also voted for Rausch. Commentators immediately asked if he had secured the backing of members of the conservative CDU of Chancellor Friedrich Merz, who has ruled out working with the AfD. Fourteen of the CDU's state MPs took part in the vote, but only five of them abstained as planned, and one unconfirmed report suggested four may have backed Rausch. Ahead of the vote, all 15 had ruled out voting for the AfD. Outside parliament, more than 300 protesters voiced their anger at the AfD's victory, and they crowded around Ulrich Siegmund as he spoke to German media. Siegmund's bid to become state premier is by no means secure. Like Rauch he will need the backing of 42 MPs in the 83-seat legislature. The BSW has refused to enter into a coalition with the AfD and has said it would instead back a non-partisan candidate for state premier and abstain in December's vote. Trump ordered the waiver of several measures under the «hellish sanctions» act against Russia and Iran... US President Donald Trump issued an executive order waiving various measures provided for under the recently enacted «hellish sanctions» act against Russia and Iran , specifically lifting the imposition of 500 percent tariffs on Russian products. «As further set forth in Section 4 of this Order, I hereby waive the application of the specific sanctions, restrictions, and tariffs provided for in the Graham Act», the document states. The President emphasized that such a decision is in the interest of the United States . According to the document, Donald Trump , specifically, waived the application of tariffs of up to 500 percent on Russian products and 100 percent tariffs against the five largest buyers of Russian oil and natural gas. On September 19 , Donald Trump signed the «Sanctions from Hell» Act, named after the late Senator Lindsey Graham . This allows him to impose additional tariffs of up to 100 percent on goods from countries ranked among the five largest buyers of Russian oil and natural gas, as well as additional tariffs of up to 500 percent on Russian goods imported into the United States . A week ago, Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump held a telephone conversation. Following the conversation, the President of the US announced a significant agreement in the energy sector: Russia , depending on the condition of its refineries, will supply up to 3 million tons of diesel to the markets of the US and global markets. For this purpose, the US Department of the Treasury issued a sanctions waiver valid until April 7, 2027 . Russian praise for Trump's decision to cancel sanctions against Russia, Stroke on global markets The suspension of the implementation of the act of the deceased Senator Lindsey Graham by the administration of Donald Trump was described as a critical and truly historic turning point in bilateral relations by the Special Representative of the Russian President for Investment and Economic Cooperation with Foreign Countries and head of the RDIF , Kirill Dmitriev . The Russian official underscored that both Washington and Moscow maintain a vital interest in economic partnership, which serves the interests of both sides. In a relevant statement on his Telegram channel, Kirill Dmitriev noted that instead of the regime of sanctions and perpetual confrontation, priority is now given to dialogue, mutually beneficial cooperation, and the consequent shared responsibility for global stability. According to the head of the RDIF , the full activation of the Lindsey Graham act carried the risk of permanently severing all economic interaction between Russia and the United States , delivering a severe blow to the American economy itself and to international markets. Kirill Dmitriev emphasized that economic cooperation between the two countries constitutes a cornerstone for the stability of the global system and the creation of a framework of trust leading to sustainable peace. Két Railjet vonatszerelvény étkezőkocsiját is feltörték keddre virradó éjjel – számolt be róla Hegyi Zsolt, a MÁV-csoport vezérigazgatója , miután a Mávinform arról tájékoztatta az utasokat, hogy rendőrségi intézkedések miatt két kedd reggeli Railjet sem indul időben Ausztria, illetve Németország irányába a Keletiből. Hegyi Zsolt elmondása szerint konkrétan arról van szó, hogy még tartott a feltört szerelvényekben a helyszínelés. Hozzátette: a történtek miatt a vasút is vizsgálatot indít. Mint írta, a kocsikat feltörők olyan károkat okoztak az utastérben, ami miatt azokat eleve nem lehetett forgalomba állítani. Arra, hogy az étkezőkocsikból el is loptak-e valamit, nem tért ki. „A vasúti üzemi területek hatalmasak, hagyományos eszközökkel szinte lehetetlen mindenhol folyamatos ellenőrzést biztosítani” – világította meg a történtek hátterét Hegyi Zsolt. Ugyanakkor azt is leszögezte, hogy ez nem jelentheti azt, hogy szabad utat engednek a rongálóknak. Emlékeztetett arra is, hogy éppen a közelmúltban jelentették be, hogy drónokkal erősítik meg a vasúti területek ellenőrzését, és ennek az iránynak a helyességét igazolják a mostanihoz hasonló esetek is. Többször előfordult az is, hogy fiatalok másztak fel vasúti kocsik tetejére, és halálos áramütést kaptak: az új technika ezt is megakadályozhatná. „Minden rendelkezésünkre álló eszközt be kell vetnünk, hogy megvédjük a járműveinket, időben észleljük a veszélyt, és tetten érjük az elkövetőket” – jelentette ki. A rendőrség a HVG megkeresésére közölte: a VIII. Kerületi Rendőrkapitányság lopás bűntett gyanúja miatt rendelt el nyomozást ismeretlen tettes ellen.

https://www.dw.com/en/germany-s-2027-bud.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5PQsi Prefer DW on Google Lawmakers worked through the night to hammer out the details of the federal budget Image: Carsten Koall/dpa/picture alliance Advertisement It was 5:55 a.m. on Friday when the Bundestag 's Budget Committee concluded its final session. Following nearly 16 hours of negotiations, lawmakers from the conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU) and Christian Social Union (CSU) parties, along with their coalition partners from the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD), voted in favor of the 2027 draft budget. The opposition parties — the environmentalist Greens , the socialist Left Party and the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) — voted against it. With that, the way is now clear for the final vote in the Bundestag on November 27. Reading through the nearly 1,000-page document requires a great deal of number-crunching. Next year, the federal government plans to spend around €561 billion ($620 billion). But here's the problem: it won't collect nearly enough revenue to cover these expenses. With a shortfall of €123 billion, borrowing will be needed to bridge the gap. Germany's slow road to recovery To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video But that's not the only problem. On top of all this debt, Germany also has loans for defense spending and for the renovation of the dilapidated infrastructure. Approved by the Bundestag in 2025, these special funds are set to be in place for multiple years. If the new debt for 2027 is factored in, the total borrowing amounts to over €210 billion. This is the second-highest level of borrowing in the history of the Federal Republic of Germany. The only time Germany borrowed more was during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2021, when borrowing reached €215.4 billion. This development has drawn sharp criticism from opposition parties. Green Party lawmaker Sebastian Schäfer and his colleague Dietmar Bartsch of the Left Party called it a "gigantic mountain of debt," an "untrustworthy" budget, "irresponsible" policies at the expense of future generations and a lack of future prospects. Why is debt growing? Crises drive up costs To understand the reasons behind the growing debt, one has to look beyond the numbers. Every federal budget is a snapshot of the priorities set by a government and a country — in terms of the economy, social issues, security and geopolitics. What are the German government's pension, labor reforms? While Russia's war against Ukraine is driving up defense spending, the faltering economy is also demanding new investments. At the same time, Germany's population is aging rapidly, which is driving up social spending. What's more, the crumbling infrastructure must be repaired and modernized, and the energy transition is costing billions. And more than half of all this debt is going toward security and defense. Defense spending continues to rise Russia's war against Ukraine will enter its sixth year in 2027. As of the end of June, the federal government estimated its overall support for Ukraine to have reached approximately €100 billion. In response to a request from the AfD in the Bundestag, the government stated: "The federal government will continue to provide Ukraine with political, financial, humanitarian, civil and military support for as long as necessary." The rearmament of the Bundeswehr and spending on NATO are also putting massive pressure on the budget. The defense budget is set to grow to just under €110 billion in 2027, an increase of around €27 billion compared to last year. Added to this are expenditures from the Bundeswehr's special fund. Largest budget item: Social spending and pensions Nevertheless, by far the largest single budget item comes from the Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs, which is set to grow to over €200 billion. There are plans for cost-cutting measures, for example, in basic income support for job seekers. But the costs of old-age pension benefits continue to rise. How risky is the German government's borrowing spree? Back then, more than 1 million children were born each year. But birth rates nearly halved in the early 1970s and have continued to decline since then. As a result, there will be an increasing number of retirees and a decreasing number of working-age individuals in the coming years. The pension funds cannot be financed by the pension contributions of this dwindling workforce and have to be subsidized by the government. Already, contributions to the pension insurance system — which are split equally between employees and employers — will have to be increased. They are expected to rise to just under 20% of gross salary. The Federal Employment Agency, too, has long been unable to make ends meet on contributions alone. In 2027, subsidies of more than €8 billion from the federal budget are planned. Germany no longer a model of fiscal discipline Anyone comparing Germany's current budget situation with that of past years will be rubbing their eyes in disbelief. It wasn't that long ago that Germany was considered a model of fiscal discipline. Between 2014 and 2019, the federal budget managed to avoid taking on new debt for six consecutive years. In some years, there was even money left over. However, today Germany is still enjoying the benefits of those years of fiscal stability. Compared to other countries, Germany is still in relatively good shape. Economic experts warn of rising debt The key indicator is not the amount of debt along but the debt-to-GDP ratio. It indicates how high the national debt is in relation to annual economic output. At the end of 2025, it stood at 63.5% for Germany. France, on the other hand, stands at over 110% and Italy at about 135% to 140%, while the US is well above 100%. However, in its latest fall report, the German Council of Economic Experts warned that Germany could be heading down a dangerous path. If debt continues to rise at this rate, the debt-to-GDP ratio could climb to 100% by 2040. This would also put Germany's creditworthiness on the financial markets at risk. Germany is the only country among the seven leading democratic industrialized nations ( G7 ) that still holds a triple-A (AAA) rating. This is the highest possible credit rating on the financial markets. It signals to investors that the risk of default on German government bonds is extremely low.
